trial_court: Principal Senior Civil Judge, Rajahmundry; Second Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Rajahmundry
case_name: Ch. Sri Rama Murthy vs Ch. Rajyalakshmi
facts_of_case: The husband filed a transfer CMP under Section 24 of the Code praying for transfer of cases to the Family Court, Visakhapatnam. The wife had filed several litigations in different Courts at Rajahmundry. The husband claimed that he was being harassed and sought relief.

legal_principles.principle: A transfer CMP cannot be maintained under Section 24 of the Code if a composite transfer CMP is filed.
legal_principles.held: The learned Counsel also had further pointed out that M.C.No. 51 of 2001 was filed on the file of the Second Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Rajahmundry under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the said proceeding under the Code of Criminal Procedure is not amenable to be transferred by exercising powers under Section 24 of the Code.

legal_principles.principle: A later O.P. filed by the husband may have to be transferred to be tried along with the prior O.P. for judicial separation.
legal_principles.held: The learned Counsel also submitted that even in view of Section 21 A of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as 'Act' in short) inasmuch as the O.P. filed by the wife for judicial separation being first in point of time, the later O.P. filed by the husband may have to be transferred to be tried along with the prior O.P. for the judicial separation.

outcome.final_order: The court granted the transfer of cases to the Family Court, Visakhapatnam.

use_for_drafting: practical tips for family court proceedings
